clues: This capital city sits on a wide gulf on the north-west coast of a Caribbean island. It has been the chief city of its island nation for ages.
Rain falls most from May to December in this city, then a dry season runs from January to April. The year thus splits into a long wet part and a short dry part.
This city has served as the capital of its island since 1757. That is a run of well over two and a half centuries in the same role.
Just before Lent each year, a vast carnival fills this city with colour and joy. It is the city's main feast of the year and its big draw for guests.
This city is home to the biggest and most winning stock market in the whole Caribbean. Traders round the area know it well for that one fact.
